Tests that URL and URLSearchParams read-only methods are side-effect-free.
Expression `URL.canParse('https://example.com/?a=1')`
has side effect: false, expected: false
Expression `URL.parse('https://example.com/?a=1').toJSON()`
has side effect: false, expected: false
Expression `JSON.stringify(URL.parse('https://example.com/?a=1'))`
has side effect: false, expected: false
Expression `URL.parse('https://example.com/?a=1').searchParams.get('a')`
has side effect: false, expected: false
Expression `URL.parse('https://example.com/?a=1').searchParams.getAll('a')`
has side effect: false, expected: false
Expression `URL.parse('https://example.com/?a=1').searchParams.has('a')`
has side effect: false, expected: false
Expression `URL.parse('https://example.com/?a=1').searchParams.set('a', '2')`
has side effect: true, expected: true
Expression `URL.parse('https://example.com/?a=1').searchParams.append('b', '3')`
has side effect: true, expected: true
Expression `URL.parse('https://example.com/?a=1').searchParams.delete('a')`
has side effect: true, expected: true
Expression `URL.parse('https://example.com/?a=1').searchParams.sort()`
has side effect: true, expected: true
